subject: Clarifying prorated session billing, context rounding, and pilot cap
messages:
From: Sara Holt <sara.holt@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on how long_context sessions are metered

Marcus —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Our procurement team wants a concise explanation of how you meter sessions that hold a long context (we're testing 64k contexts) vs. short sessions. A few specific items our finance folks asked for: 

- Do you bill context (input) tokens and generation (output) tokens differently for rounding? If so, what are the quantum sizes (e.g., rounded to nearest 10/25/100 tokens)?
- How do you treat an idle long-lived session (session that keeps the KV cache but receives no generations for 20 hours)? Is the daily/session minimum applied?
- If we negotiated a % discount on list unit rates, does it apply before or after any session minimums / rounding adjustments?
- Can you provide a short example invoice line for: (a) a 64k prompt + 1k generated tokens, (b) a short request with 150 input + 30 output tokens, and (c) a long-lived session that has 0 outputs for a day but remains warm in your routing layer.

I'm attaching a short doc with the procurement checklist. We're on a tight timeline; procurement review is next Tuesday.

Appreciate the clarity —
Sara Holt
Head of Procurement, Acme Corp
Attach: acme_pricing_questions.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Holt <sara.holt@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on how long_context sessions are metered

Sara —

Thanks, great questions. Below is a short, practical summary and then three worked examples to match your ask. If you want a single-page appendix for procurement I can convert this into a one-pager.

Summary (short):
- We meter both input (context) and output (generation) tokens.
- Rounding: context (input) tokens are rounded up in 8-token increments; generation (output) tokens are rounded up in 10-token increments.
- Session minimums: we apply a per-session active-day minimum (500 tokens equivalent) per 24-hour active window. An "active window" is any 24-hour period in which the session recorded at least one generation token. If a session remains warm but receives zero generation tokens during the 24h window, the minimum is NOT charged.
- Discounts: negotiated percentage discounts apply to the billed token rates after rounding/quantization but before applying any credits or one-time concessions. In other words, rounding -> compute token counts -> apply discount to unit rate -> sum lines -> apply credits.

Examples (rounded and then billed):
1) 64k prompt + 1k generated tokens (single request):
   - Context tokens = 64,000 -> rounded up to nearest 8-token quantum = 64,000 (already multiple of 8)
   - Generation tokens = 1,000 -> rounded up to 10-token quantum = 1,000
   - Token counts billed: input 64,000, output 1,000 -> discount applies to unit price on each line
2) Short request (150 input + 30 output):
   - Context 150 -> rounded up to 152 (8-token increments)
   - Generation 30 -> rounded up to 30 (10-token quantum -> 30)
   - If total generation tokens for the session's 24-hour active window fall below 500, we apply session minimum by billing the difference to reach 500 generation-equivalent tokens. (We translate input tokens to generation-equivalent using a standard factor for minimums; for simplicity procurement docs use generation-equivalent = generation tokens + floor(input_tokens/4).)
3) Long-lived warm session with 0 outputs for 24 hours:
   - No generation tokens => not an active window => session minimum NOT charged.

Notes: the minimum is intended to prevent per-session tiny charges when there is measurable generation activity. Warm-only state (KV cached, no generations) does not trigger the minimum.

Let me know if you want these in a sample invoice format. I'm copying Marissa (AE) so she can coordinate a pilot concession if needed.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Platform Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Holt <sara.holt@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Fri, 3 Jun 2028 13:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on how long_context sessions are metered

Thanks Marcus — that helps. A couple follow-ups so procurement can close the review: 

- For the session-minimum calculation, can you run the sample math for our expected traffic pattern? For pilot week 1 we expect 40 sessions that generate occasional outputs: 28 sessions average 200 generation tokens/day, 12 sessions average 0 generation tokens/day but stay warm. Will you show how minimums would apply?
- On discounts: our legal/commercial team expects the negotiated 30% to apply to the final billed lines; your statement that discount applies after rounding is acceptable, but will this interact with minimums in ways that make the effective discount lower? Example: if rounding pushes a small request over the 500 token min, we want to ensure the discount isn't applied after you already forced the session into the minimum.

If you can provide a one-page worked example for the pilot (numbers above) and confirm whether Redwood will consider waiving the session minimum for the pilot period, procurement can sign off next week.

Sara
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Holt <sara.holt@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Jun 2028 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on how long_context sessions are metered

Sara —

Appreciate the concrete pilot numbers. Quick answers and then a proposed path forward: 

1) Worked example (pilot week, 40 sessions):
   - 28 sessions @ 200 generation tokens/day -> generation rounded: 200 -> 200 (10-token quantum) each = 28 * 200 = 5,600 generation tokens/day billed.
   - 12 sessions @ 0 generation tokens/day but warm -> not active windows -> no session minimum.
   - Session minimum only applies to sessions that record >0 generation tokens within the 24h window. So none of the 28 sessions individually hit the 500-token minimum; however, we apply session-level minimum by charging the difference up to 500 for any session whose generation tokens < 500. For each of your 28 sessions: billed generation tokens per session becomes max(200,500) = 500 -> so billed generation tokens = 28 * 500 = 14,000.
   - Effective generations billed/day across the 28 sessions = 14,000 (after minimums).
   - Rounding & discounts: rounding happens first (we rounded to quantum above), then discount (30%) applies to the billed token counts * unit price. This means the minimum increases billed token count before discount; the discount reduces the monetary impact but does not change the token counts used to determine minimum thresholds.

2) Pilot concession proposal:
   - Given this is a pilot and to avoid surprising procurement, Redwood will waive the per-session minimum for the first 90 days for Acme pilot if Acme agrees to a pilot cap on daily spend. Proposed cap: $1,200/day.
   - Operational detail: during the 90-day waiver we will still report session-level usage (so you can see how minimums would have applied), but we will not invoice the minimums. Token rounding and the discount still apply to actual billed lines.

3) Next steps:
   - If you accept the waiver + cap, we'll include a SOW amendment that states: 90-day session-minimum waiver for pilot, daily invoice cap of $1,200, and standard 30% negotiated discount applies to all billed token lines.
   - I copied Vanessa from Finance to confirm accounting/process for the cap/waiver and Marissa to get the SOW drafted.

If that looks reasonable I'll have the SOW draft and a one-page worked example back to you within 24 hours.

Thanks —
Marcus
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Holt <sara.holt@acme.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Sara —

Happy to proceed with the 90-day waiver + $1,200/day cap. Vanessa — can you confirm we can execute this as a one-line SOW amendment and issue the first invoice with pilot cap applied? I'll attach the SOW draft for your review (SOW_draft_acme_20280604.docx).
